blinding.$comment: A hit rate materially above chance does not void the comparison; it attaches a caveat to it, and the caveat is never omitted.

$comment: What is fixed here is the *operator's* typing, not the platform's work. An assumption the
platform derives — a beta from prices, a risk-free rate from the published series at the
run's vintage, a growth or margin intensity from the filings — must be allowed to derive,
because that derivation is the product being measured. Freezing it would measure a
constant.
What must not vary is a number somebody typed, because two runs that differ only in the
operator's typing produce two valuations and no information.
Read off the re-seeded corpus on 19 September 2026, which showed why this row exists:
MSFT's approved run carried a hand-typed beta of 0.900 where the platform had derived
1.068 from prices, and AZN's carried a hand-typed 0.300 — implausibly low for a
pharmaceutical company and, on the evidence, a placeholder nobody revisited. Either
number would have made this round's valuation a measurement of the typing.
assumptions.rule: Prefer the platform's own derived value wherever it can derive one. Where it cannot, the operator supplies the value named below, identically in every run of the round.

corrections_from_the_corpus.subject: msft
corrections_from_the_corpus.why: The platform derived 1.068 for the same subject in the other run. A typed 0.900 overrides the product with a guess, at the single most leveraged input to the discount rate.

corrections_from_the_corpus.subject: azn
corrections_from_the_corpus.why: 0.300 is far below any plausible pharmaceutical beta and no justification in the record defends it. Left in, the round's AZN valuation would be indefensible for a reason that has nothing to do with what the round is measuring.
